explication:
<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - This is a native Swift image‐loading framework (not a full-stack app).  
   - It provides a core “ImagePipeline” (Sources/Nuke) plus three higher-level modules:  
     • NukeUI – SwiftUI & UIKit/AppKit image views  
     • NukeExtensions – convenience extensions for UIImageView/AppKit  
     • NukeVideo – video decoding & playback helpers  

2. Analyze the file structure  
   - Top-level directories:  
     • .scripts – CI, linting, testing, build helpers  
     • Documentation – guides, API docs, migration notes  
     • Sources – four modules: Nuke, NukeUI, NukeExtensions, NukeVideo  
     • Tests – thousands of unit, performance, thread-safety, UI tests  
   - Inside Sources/Nuke: clearly defined subpackages for Caching, Decoding, Encoding, Loading, Pipeline orchestration, Prefetching, Processing, Tasks, Internal utilities  

3. Extract architectural clues from README  
   - Core abstraction: ImagePipeline + ImageTask + ImageRequest + ImageResponse  
   - Key features: memory/disk cache, request coalescing, priority, progressive JPEG, async/await & Combine, extensibility points (plugins for networking, codecs)  

4. How to draw the system design diagram  
   a. Main components (boxes):  
      1. Client UI Layer  
         – SwiftUI (LazyImage) / UIKit (ImageView) via NukeUI  
         – UIImageView extensions via NukeExtensions  
      2. Core Image Pipeline  
         – ImagePipeline façade  
         – Task Manager (coalescing, priority)  
         – ImageTask / AsyncPipelineTask  
      3. Cache Layer  
         – MemoryCache (in-memory)  
         – DataCache (disk)  
      4. Data Loading Layer  
         – Default URLSessionDataLoader  
         – Pluggable DataLoader protocol for custom networking (Alamofire plugin)  
      5. Decoding Layer  
         – ImageDecoderRegistry → built-in decoders (JPEG, PNG, WebP, HEIF, etc.)  
      6. Processing Layer  
         – ImageProcessors (resize, blur, circle, composition, custom)  
      7. Encoding Layer (optional)  
         – ImageEncoders (for disk, or re-upload)  
      8. Prefetcher  
         – ImagePrefetcher coordinates ahead-of-time fetching  
      9. External Services / Plugins (optional)  
         – Networking plugin (Alamofire)  
         – Format plugins (WebP, AVIF)  
   b. Relationships & data flows (arrows):  
      • UI → calls ImagePipeline.shared.imageTask(with: request)  
      • Pipeline → 1) check MemoryCache → 2) check Disk DataCache → 3) if miss, invoke DataLoader → 4) publish raw Data → 5) pass through Decoding → 6) pass through Processing → 7) update Caches → 8) return ImageResponse to UI  
      • Prefetcher → enqueues requests directly into Pipeline (skips UI)  
      • Extensions & Plugins → registered with Pipeline or DataLoader via protocols  
   c. Architectural patterns & principles:  
      – Facade (ImagePipeline hides complexity)  
      – Strategy / Registry (pluggable Decoders, DataLoaders, Processors)  
      – Composite (cache hierarchy: memory + disk)  
      – Publisher/Subscriber (Combine or AsyncSequence for progress & events)  
      – Singletons (ImagePipeline.shared) but fully configurable  
   d. Key technologies & frameworks:  
      – Swift 5+ (async/await, actors)  
      – Combine for publisher-based APIs  
      – UIKit, AppKit & SwiftUI for UI layers  
      – URLSession (default networking)  
      – AVFoundation / VideoToolbox for NukeVideo  

5. Tailoring the diagram to this library project  
   - Emphasize module boundaries: show four distinct modules (Nuke, NukeUI, NukeExtensions, NukeVideo)  
   - Highlight core pipeline internals in detail (caching, loading, decoding, processing) since that is the “heart”  
   - Show UI modules as thin wrappers that call into the core  
   - Represent external plugin points off to the side  

6. Diagramming guidelines  
   - Use clear, descriptive labels on each box (e.g., “MemoryCache”, “ImageDecoderRegistry”)  
   - Draw uni-directional arrows to indicate the flow of data (Data → Decoding → Processing → Cache → UI)  
   - Color-code:  
     • Blue for core pipeline components  
     • Green for UI modules (NukeUI / NukeExtensions)  
     • Orange for extension/plugin points  
     • Grey for scripts, documentation, tests (if shown)  
   - Use cylinder icons for cache layers (representing memory & disk)  
   - Use cloud icon or external box for networking layer  

7. Level of detail  
   - Don’t just show “Pipeline” – break out sub-components (Cache, Loader, Decoder, Processor)  
   - Include the Prefetcher and Task orchestration as separate components  
   - Annotate extension points (DataLoaderProtocol, ImageDecoderProtocol, ProcessorProtocol) to emphasize customizability  
   - Optionally, overlay numbering on the arrows to show the sequence of operations (1…8)  

By following these guidelines you will produce a clear, accurate system design diagram that reflects both the high-level module organization and the detailed flow of image requests through the Nuke framework.
</explanation>
